After doing a "lake update" this morning, "lake build" fails with

✖ [640/916] Building proofwidgets/widgetJsAll
error: ProofWidgets not up-to-date. Please run lake exe cache get to fetch the latest ProofWidgets. If this does not work, report your issue on the Lean Zulip.
Some required targets logged failures:
- proofwidgets/widgetJsAll
error: build failed

I tried "lake exe cache get", but since this did not help, I report the issue here.
In what context are you running lake update? Is this your own project or are you contributing to Mathlib?

Dear Mac, thanks for asking. This is my own project,

  • https://github.com/kebekus/ProjectVD

… which worked well yesterday.

There was a recent issue with a ProofWidgets update in Mathlib. You may have updated at an inopportune time. I would suggest the following to try and get into a fixed state:

  • Run lake update again to make sure you are on latest Mathlib.
  • Delete the .lake directory to remove any potentially corrupted Lake files.
  • Run lake exe cache get! (the execlamation mark is important) to clobber any potential corruption in cache.
  • Run lake build to test if everything now works.
Will do.
@Mac Malone The procedure did indeed fix the issue for me. Thank you for your help!

I also would like to say that I am experiencing issues with ProofWidgets at basically any single toolchain update (it happened again today while working on a mathlib branch, maybe because of the upgrade to lean4:v4.29.0-rc7?). The error message suggesting running lake exe cache get is not helpful.

I had the same issue as @Stefan Kebekus , but in my mathlib folder. Running lake exe cache get! hadn't sufficed, but deleting .lake and following the rest of the procedure given by @Mac Malone worked.
Same here one minute ago.
I ran into the same thing and deleting .lake and running lake exe cache get! afterwards fixed it for me as well.

If anyone else encounters this issue, it would be nice to get a copy of the broken .lake directory. It is not quite clear what happened here and being able to compare a functional directory with a broken directory would help with debugging. Ideally, this could be preventing from occuring in the future.
It would also be interesting to learn if lake clean instead of rm -rf .lake is sufficient to fix the issue.
There was a report at #mathlib4 > ✓CI failure: proofwidgets/widgetJsAll @ 💬 that lake clean did not work (but deleting .lake did).

@Mac Malone, it's pretty trivial to reproduce:

rm -rf .lake
git checkout 5215e9b0d4
lake exe cache get
git checkout 276bbda7c2
lake build proofwidgets/widgetJsAll

The last one fails with 

✖ [226/508] Building proofwidgets/widgetJsAll
error: ProofWidgets not up-to-date. Please run `lake exe cache get` to fetch the latest ProofWidgets. If this does not work, report your issue on the Lean Zulip.

and continues failing after lake clean or lake exe cache get!, but rm -rf .lake fixes it.
Ah, thanks!
(Those commits are just master~100 and master a moment ago.)

Sorry, there's been some confusion about reproducing this problem.

Could I have someone run these steps and confirm for me that they fully reproduce the problem?

rm -rf /tmp/mathlib4-pw-repro
git clone https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4.git /tmp/mathlib4-pw-repro
cd /tmp/mathlib4-pw-repro
git checkout 5215e9b0d498e4ce8d6787d82fe52e8f0df31dc5
lake exe cache get
lake build Mathlib.Tactic.Common
git checkout 276bbda7c2ab277ae1582c27f8aa8bfa3fed4c9c
lake exe cache get
lake build Mathlib.Tactic.Common
lake clean
lake exe cache get
lake build Mathlib.Tactic.Common
lake exe cache 'get!'
lake build Mathlib.Tactic.Common
rm -rf .lake
lake exe cache get
lake build Mathlib.Tactic.Common

Here we expect the first and last lake build to succeed, but all three intermediate lake builds to fail with error: ProofWidgets not up-to-date.

I've also rewritten a script that runs all these steps for you, and validates their outputs/exit codes. You can run it with:

curl -fsSL https://gist.githubusercontent.com/kim-em/179ba26368e596d1116c13171e28656a/raw/repro.sh | bash

(obviously you should load the URL in a browser first and skim through it to see it doesn't do anything insane)

For me, it produces the following output:

============================================

$ rm -rf /tmp/mathlib4-pw-repro
$ git clone https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4.git /tmp/mathlib4-pw-repro
--> ok

Step 1: Cache get and build at old commit (PW v0.0.92, rc6)
$ git checkout 5215e9b0d498e4ce8d6787d82fe52e8f0df31dc5
--> ok
$ lake exe cache get
--> ok
$ lake build Mathlib.Tactic.Common
--> ok

Step 2: Switch to new commit (PW v0.0.93, rc7), cache get, build -- fails
$ git checkout 276bbda7c2ab277ae1582c27f8aa8bfa3fed4c9c
--> ok
$ lake exe cache get
--> ok
$ lake build Mathlib.Tactic.Common
--> ok (failed as expected: error: ProofWidgets not up-to-date. Please run lake exe cache get to fetch the latest ProofWidgets. If this does not work, report your issue on the Lean Zulip.)

Step 3: lake clean + cache get does not fix it
$ lake clean
--> ok
$ lake exe cache get
--> ok
$ lake build Mathlib.Tactic.Common
--> ok (failed as expected: error: ProofWidgets not up-to-date. Please run lake exe cache get to fetch the latest ProofWidgets. If this does not work, report your issue on the Lean Zulip.)

Step 4: lake exe cache get! does not fix it
$ lake exe cache get!
--> ok
$ lake build Mathlib.Tactic.Common
--> ok (failed as expected: error: ProofWidgets not up-to-date. Please run lake exe cache get to fetch the latest ProofWidgets. If this does not work, report your issue on the Lean Zulip.)

Step 5: rm -rf .lake + cache get fixes it
$ rm -rf .lake
$ lake exe cache get
--> ok
$ lake build Mathlib.Tactic.Common
--> ok

============================================

Bug reproduced successfully.

Nice, thanks! I think we know what's going on now, back soon.

Okay, and here's a new version of the repro script that I think demonstrates the problem is due to a stale package-lock.json.hash file:

curl -fsSL https://gist.githubusercontent.com/kim-em/b53403565687dd6b81238809472271d5/raw/repro.sh | bash

Note that this script also validates that lake build -H is sufficient to fix the problem.
